page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadsv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is provisioned with 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 3780 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test and single-threaded gzip compression both rank in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-threaded decompression and PassMark CPU scores are strong, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks fall into the average tier. For machine learning workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds with small LLM models, but performance degrades significantly on larger models, with 70B model text generation falling into the bottom 10%.

Given its high memory density of 16 GB per core and large local NVMe SSD storage, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require proportional scaling of compute cores. It is well-suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems, data warehousing, and memory-heavy enterprise applications. The lack of GPU acceleration and poor large-model LLM inference performance make it unsuitable for heavy deep learning training or large-scale AI generation, but it remains highly effective for high-throughput static web serving and single-threaded data processing tasks.

The hardware profile includes 512.0 GB of RAM (16.0 GB per core) and a bundled 3780 GB NVMe SSD for high-speed local storage, with no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show top-tier single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression, alongside strong PassMark CPU and memory scores. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth remain average, and large-model LLM inference is poor. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, in-memory caching, and static web serving, offering strong resource density for workloads requiring massive memory capacity relative to compute cores.
